rationale: The reviewed plan remains broadly spec-faithful and the unchanged R4 checks pass, but the round-6 empty-diff fix is only partial. Trailer-encoded kinds make existing C and D commits unambiguous, yet eliding a stage also elides the durable evidence that the stage ran. After a no-op S, for example, tip and marker still identify C; a crash before merge is therefore indistinguishable from a crash immediately after C, and the prescribed re-entry runs R and S again. The symmetric empty-C window can replay R, and if both commits are elided there is no marker at all. Fixtures xv-xvii do not cover these post-elision crash boundaries. This is a load-bearing recovery-state defect that can direct bead 6 to implement a false run-once protocol, so the plan should not pass until the elision/replay contract is made mechanically honest.
concrete_changes_required: Give every completed M/S boundary durable, unambiguous recovery evidence even when its tree is unchanged (for example, retain trailer-bearing empty C/D commits or specify equivalent persistent stage state), OR explicitly replace the run-exactly-once claim with a replay-safe at-least-once protocol and prove every replayed operation is idempotent and preserves the convergence contract.

Extend the bead-6 failure fixtures to interrupt (a) after R when C was elided but before any D publication, (b) after a no-op S/D elision but before merge, and (c) when both C and D are elided. Assert the chosen truthful contract: either R/S are not replayed, or replay is explicitly permitted and proven safe. Keep fixture xvii's ordinary-D trailer classification coverage.

findings.summary: Round 6's discriminator ask is addressed for commits that exist: Mindspec-Stage trailers distinguish materialization from artifact-sync without consulting ambiguous tree diffs. It is not addressed for elided stages, because no durable observation records that an elided stage completed.

No-op D elision contradicts the claimed R/S run-once reconciliation. After C is published and advanced, S may run and elide D because the artifact is unchanged. Until merge/terminal clear, the durable state remains tip==marker==C. A crash there re-enters through the C trailer and runs R then S again; it cannot distinguish post-C/pre-R from post-S/pre-merge.

Empty-C elision has the symmetric missing-boundary problem: before a later D marker is published, a crash after R leaves no materialization marker and a rerun can repeat R. If C and D are both elided, no stage marker exists at all. Trailer readability cannot recover a stage for which no commit object was created.

Fixture xv covers empty-C classification only generically and does not pin the crash after R/before D-publication window. Fixture xvi kills after A-to-C and proves the pre-S resume path, but does not kill after no-op S before merge, where the ambiguity occurs. Fixture xvii adequately pins ordinary artifact-changing D classification.
